label: original-phase token (n/k/f/p/o/x...) following recent t/v/w/k/i inputs
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at positions 2-8 (98.7% of mass; never at t=0,1, never on the delimiter, very rarely in the copy phase). It behaves like a soft conjunction of a recency-weighted history and the current input. History part: recent inputs (prev_tok / prev2_tok / 3 back) from {t,v,w,k,i}, with t by far the strongest (prev2_tok=t lift 7.3x). Current-input part: n (6x), k, f, p, o, x, then 1, d, u, q. It favors first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 holds 89% of mass). Requiring at least 2 of the last 3 inputs from the history set plus a current input from the list gives dev F1 0.43 (precision 0.50, recall 0.37, mass recall 0.52). Coverage is much higher for the top activation quartile (about 0.7) than the bottom one, so stronger activations line up with more of both conditions holding. Looser versions (1 recent trigger) reach mass recall 0.84-0.93 but precision drops to 0.14-0.17. The rest of the activation looks like a graded, additive mix of these token weights that no crisp boolean rule captures.
